questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney's visit to India on 2 March 2026:
1. The two countries signed Terms of Reference to launch negotiations on a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA).
2. They set a target of bilateral trade of USD 100 billion by 2030.
3. The Department of Atomic Energy signed a USD 2.6 billion long-term uranium supply contract with Cameco.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The CEPA target is USD 50 billion of bilateral trade by 2030, up from USD 8.7 billion in 2024-25, so statement 2 inflates it. Canada is a major uranium supplier, and the Cameco contract supports India's nuclear power programme. A critical-minerals MoU aligned with the G7 Critical Minerals Action Plan was also signed.
questions.s: Drishti IAS / PRS / India Briefing, 2 Mar 2026

questions.q: During Finnish President Alexander Stubb's state visit to India (4-7 March 2026), India and Finland elevated their ties to:
o: a Strategic Partnership in Digitalisation and Sustainability
a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership in Defence and Space
a Special Strategic Partnership in Green Hydrogen
a Free Trade Partnership with the EFTA bloc
questions.e: Outcomes included MoUs on migration and mobility, a Joint Task Force on 6G and an Indo-Finland Startup Corridor, with both sides aiming to double trade by 2030. Stubb was also chief guest at the 11th Raisina Dialogue. The upgrade is to a strategic partnership, not a comprehensive or special strategic one.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the 11th Raisina Dialogue held in New Delhi in March 2026:
1. Its theme was 'Samskara - Assertion, Accommodation, Advancement'.
2. It is organised by NITI Aayog with the Observer Research Foundation.
3. It launched a Raisina Science Diplomacy Initiative.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Raisina Dialogue is India's flagship geopolitics conference, held annually since 2016 by the Ministry of External Affairs together with the Observer Research Foundation, so statement 2 wrongly names NITI Aayog. The 2026 edition was inaugurated by the Prime Minister.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the 7th Joint Committee Meeting under the India-Japan CEPA, held on 2 March 2026:
1. It was held in Tokyo to review implementation and promote more balanced trade.
2. The India-Japan CEPA took effect in August 2011.
3. Japan is India's largest source of foreign direct investment.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Japan is India's fifth-largest source of FDI, with USD 43.2 billion cumulative from 2000 to December 2024, so it is not the largest. The CEPA came into force in August 2011, and bilateral trade stood at USD 22.85 billion in 2023-24.

questions.q: Which one of the following correctly describes the outcome of the 14th WTO Ministerial Conference (MC14)?
o: It was held at Abu Dhabi and ended without consensus, so the e-commerce duty moratorium lapsed
It was held at Yaounde, Cameroon and agreed by consensus to make the e-commerce duty moratorium permanent
It was held at Yaounde, Cameroon and adopted the permanent solution on public stockholding sought by India
It was held at Yaounde, Cameroon and ended without consensus, so the e-commerce duty moratorium in place since 1998 lapsed
questions.e: MC14 ran from 26 to 29 March 2026 and closed in the early hours of 30 March; talks moved to the General Council in Geneva. The lapse of the moratorium after 26 years means members can now impose customs duties on electronic transmissions. India had sought a permanent solution on public stockholding for food security, which was not delivered.
questions.s: Down To Earth / Drishti IAS, 30 Mar 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Investment Facilitation for Development (IFD) Agreement at the WTO:
1. India, South Africa, Turkiye and about 37 other members objected to incorporating it into the WTO framework.
2. It is a multilateral agreement originally negotiated by developing countries led by India.
3. Incorporating a plurilateral agreement into the WTO framework requires consensus among members.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The IFD is a China-backed plurilateral initiative, not an Indian-led one. Objectors cited erosion of consensus-based decision-making, plurilateralism and policy sovereignty. India links its stand to a permanent solution on Public Stockholding under the Doha agenda; adding a plurilateral to the WTO annexes needs consensus, which these objections block.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding India and the International Energy Agency (IEA) in March 2026:
1. India joined the IEA's coordinated release of strategic petroleum reserves.
2. The IEA agreed a record release of 400 million barrels.
3. India is a full member of the IEA.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: India declined to join the call at first and said on 11 March it 'stands ready to take appropriate measures'. India is an associate, not a full, member of the IEA. India's strategic reserves (about 5.33 million tonnes at Visakhapatnam, Mangaluru and Padur) were about 80% full.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the sinking of the Iranian frigate IRIS Dena on 4 March 2026:
1. It was sunk by a US Navy submarine in the Indian Ocean off Galle, Sri Lanka.
2. It was returning from the International Fleet Review 2026 at Kochi.
3. Sri Lanka's navy carried out rescue operations.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The ship was returning from the International Fleet Review 2026 at Visakhapatnam, not Kochi, so statement 2 is wrong. The incident raises questions under the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea and the 1979 SAR Convention, which India ratified in 2001.

questions.q:
The US Trade Representative launched two Section 301 investigations on 11 and 12 March 2026 under the Trade Act, 1974. Consider the following statements:
1. One concerns structural excess industrial capacity among 16 partners, including India.
2. The other concerns goods made with forced labour, covering 60 economies including India.
3. The probes followed the US Supreme Court striking down emergency-powers (reciprocal) tariffs.
4. They were launched after a WTO panel ruled against India.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Section 301 is a US domestic law tool; the probes were not triggered by any WTO panel ruling. With the emergency-powers tariffs struck down, the USTR turned to Section 301 investigations as an alternative legal basis. India said it remained engaged in negotiating a framework trade agreement under the February 2026 joint statement.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke to Iran's President Ebrahim Raisi on 12 March 2026 about the safety of Indian nationals.
2. The Strait of Hormuz lies between Iran and Oman and links the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman.
3. Several Gulf energy producers declared force majeure on oil and gas shipments in March 2026 after shipping through the Strait was disrupted.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Iran's President is Masoud Pezeshkian, and it was he who spoke to Modi on 12 March; Ebrahim Raisi is no longer in office. About 1 crore Indians live in GCC countries, and the Strait carries about 20 million barrels of crude a day and 20-30% of global LNG, which explains India's concern for unhindered transit.

questions.q: Which one of the following correctly gives the seats won in Nepal's House of Representatives (275 seats) in the 5 March 2026 parliamentary elections?
o: Rastriya Swatantra Party 182, CPN (UML) 38, Nepali Congress 25
Nepali Congress 182, Rastriya Swatantra Party 38, CPN (UML) 25
Rastriya Swatantra Party 182, Nepali Congress 38, CPN (UML) 25
Rastriya Swatantra Party 165, Nepali Congress 38, CPN (UML) 25
questions.e: The RSP won a commanding majority, with the Nepali Congress second and K.P. Sharma Oli's CPN (UML) third. The RSP's Balendra Shah was later sworn in as prime minister on 27 March 2026.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Balendra Shah:
1. He was sworn in as Nepal's prime minister on 27 March 2026 by President Ram Chandra Paudel.
2. At 35, he became Nepal's youngest prime minister.
3. He leads a government of the CPN (UML).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Shah belongs to the Rastriya Swatantra Party, which won 182 of 275 seats; CPN (UML) finished third. He is Nepal's 47th prime minister and is described as its first Madhesi prime minister.
questions.s: Al Jazeera / Times of Oman, 27 Mar 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Pakistan's 'Operation Ghazab Lil Haq' of March 2026:
1. It was launched against Afghan Taliban positions.
2. It followed clashes over border fencing along the 4,096 km Durand Line.
3. The Durand Line was agreed in 1893 between Sir Mortimer Durand and Emir Abdur Rahman Khan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Durand Line runs for about 2,640 km, not 4,096 km (a figure closer to the India-Bangladesh border). Pakistan began fencing it in 2017, and clashes also involve the Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan.

questions.q: India's BRICS presidency in 2026 is being held under the theme:
o: 'Strengthening Partnership for Peace and Inclusive Growth'
'Global South for a Multipolar World Order'
'Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability'
questions.e: The theme spells out the acronym BRICS: Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability. BRICS+ now includes Egypt, UAE, Ethiopia, Indonesia and Iran, and the bloc accounts for about 49.5% of world population and about 40% of global GDP.
questions.h: The theme is the acronym: B-R-I-C-S

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Indian Ocean Naval Symposium (IONS):
1. India is the Chair of IONS for 2026-2028, for the first time since the forum began.
2. The Philippines joined as the latest IONS observer in 2026.
3. IONS was launched in 2008 on the initiative of the Indian Navy.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: India returns as Chair after a 16-year gap, so 2026 is a return and not a first; India launched the forum in 2008 and chaired it at the outset. The Indian Navy also hosted the IONS Maritime Exercise (IMEX) table-top exercise at Kochi in 2026.

questions.q: The India-EFTA Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement (TEPA) completed two years since signing in March 2026. EFTA consists of:
questions.e: EFTA was founded in 1960 by the Stockholm Convention and has its secretariat in Geneva. Unlike the European Union, it is not a customs union. Sweden, Denmark, Austria and others left EFTA when they joined the EU.

questions.q:
Statement-I: India rejected the latest report of the US Commission on International Religious Freedom (USCIRF) as 'motivated and biased' in March 2026.
Statement-II: The recommendations of USCIRF, a US federal advisory body, are binding on the US government.
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: USCIRF again sought to designate India a 'country of particular concern', but it is only an advisory body and its recommendations are non-binding on the US government, so Statement-II is incorrect. The designation power rests with the US Secretary of State.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding India-China border trade through Lipulekh Pass:
1. Trade through Lipulekh Pass (Pithoragarh, Uttarakhand) is set to resume in June 2026 after a six-year halt.
2. Nepal opposed the move and reasserted its claim over Kalapani-Lipulekh-Limpiyadhura.
3. Shipki La and Nathu La, the other passes agreed for reopening in August 2025, are in Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh respectively.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Shipki La is in Himachal Pradesh and Nathu La in Sikkim, so statement 3 is wrong. Nepal's claim rests on the 1816 Treaty of Sugauli, which fixed the Kali river as the boundary.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding India's food-security assistance in March 2026:
1. India sent 1,000 metric tonnes of rice to Malawi after an El Nino-linked drought.
2. India sent 500 metric tonnes of rice to Mozambique after severe flooding.
3. The capital of Mozambique is Lusaka.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Mozambique's capital is Maputo; Lusaka is the capital of Zambia. Malawi's capital is Lilongwe, and the country is landlocked in southeastern Africa.

questions.q: The GlobE Network, whose 12th Steering Committee Meeting India hosted in New Delhi in 2026, is a network of anti-corruption law-enforcement authorities with its secretariat provided by:
o: the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC)
the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
questions.e: The network has 135 member countries. India's central authority is the Ministry of Home Affairs, with the CBI and the Enforcement Directorate as Indian member authorities. UNODC also serves as the secretariat of the UN Convention against Corruption.

questions.q: The 70th session of the UN Commission on the Status of Women (CSW-70) was held in March 2026. The CSW is a functional commission of:
questions.e: The CSW was established on 21 June 1946 and has 45 member states elected for four-year terms. It is a subsidiary of ECOSOC, not of the General Assembly or the Security Council. India was represented by the Minister of State for Women and Child Development.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. US and Israeli strikes in March 2026 hit Iran's Kharg Island, which handles about 90% of Iran's crude exports.
2. Iran retaliated by striking oil facilities at Fujairah in the UAE.
3. Fujairah lies on the Persian Gulf coast of the UAE, inside the Strait of Hormuz.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Fujairah is on the Gulf of Oman coast, outside the Strait of Hormuz, which is why the Habshan-Fujairah pipeline lets UAE crude bypass the Strait. Fujairah is also the world's second-largest ship bunkering hub after Singapore.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Lebanon in March 2026:
1. Israeli airstrikes destroyed the Qasmiyeh Bridge over the Litani River in southern Lebanon.
2. UN Security Council Resolution 1701 (2006) requires the area between the Blue Line and the Litani to be free of armed personnel other than the Lebanese government and UNIFIL.
3. UN Security Council Resolution 1701 first created UNIFIL in 1978.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: UNIFIL was created in 1978 by earlier resolutions (425 and 426); Resolution 1701 of 2006 ended the 2006 Lebanon war and strengthened its mandate. Israel sought a security zone up to the Litani.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Preah Vihear Temple:
1. Heavy fighting between Cambodia and Thailand damaged the temple.
2. The International Court of Justice awarded the temple to Thailand in 1962.
3. UNESCO listed it as a World Heritage Site in 2008.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The ICJ awarded the temple to Cambodia in 1962, so statement 2 is wrong. It is a roughly 1,000-year-old Khmer Hindu Shiva temple, and all five gateway pavilions (gopuras) were damaged in clashes in late 2025 and early 2026.

questions.q:
Arrange the following March 2026 events in chronological order:
A. Prime Minister Modi spoke to Iran's President on the West Asia conflict
B. India and Canada signed Terms of Reference for CEPA negotiations
C. Balendra Shah was sworn in as Nepal's prime minister
D. Nepal held parliamentary elections
questions.e: The CEPA Terms of Reference were signed on 2 March, Nepal voted on 5 March, Modi spoke to Pezeshkian on 12 March and Shah took the oath on 27 March.
